current_activity: a patrol of the 273d Infantry crosses the Elbe by boat near Strehla and meets Soviet soldiers, the first contact
notes: Event date: 25 April 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 19 p. 450-453: Lt. Kotzebue's patrol went beyond the Mulde to Kuehren and, on the morning of 25 April, east through Dahlen to the Elbe a few hundred yards north of Strehla, where five of his men rowed across and met Soviet soldiers of the 175th Regiment; his message was signed at 1330; Lt. Robertson's patrol met Soviet soldiers at the Torgau bridge about forty-five minutes later; Wikipedia, Elbe Day: the first documented contact took place on the morning of 25 April near Strehla, the best-known meeting later that day at Torgau). Event definition: the first contact between American and Soviet forces, made by a patrol of the division's 273d Infantry; the division commander met the Soviet commander at Torgau at 1600 on 26 April (p. 456). The row is the place of the contact, not the headquarters. Relationship: V Corps unspecified_subordination (from 7 Feb 45 to 27 Apr 45, CMH table); First Army assigned (from 7 Feb 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 18 Jan 45, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier unspecified_subordination relation to V Corps (CR0438) is closed at 27 April 1945 (assignment_table); see the Review note on it. Location: Strehla on the Elbe, the town standing for the crossing point a few hundred yards to its north; the second meeting, at the Torgau bridge (about 28 km down the river), is named in the notes only. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Strehla. Event support: strong (the Green Book and Wikipedia agree on the day and on Strehla). Location support: good (named town; the Green Book puts the crossing at the Elbe a few hundred yards north of it). Context: Wikipedia puts the first contact "on the morning of 25 April"; the Green Book (p. 450-452) has the patrol set out early and the message signed at 1330, and says that the second meeting, Robertson's at Torgau, came about 45 minutes after Craig's contact (p. 454); the hour of the first contact is not stated in the passages read, so no time is recorded. Context (27 October 2026, spot check): the regimental history of the 273d Infantry (R584) puts Kotzebue's patrol at Leckwitz near Strehla at 1130 on 25 April, Robertson's patrol on the Torgau bridge at 1600 and Craig's patrol at Clanzschwitz at 1645, and gives the first patrol as 11 men (a photograph caption says 36) where the Green Book says Kotzebue and five men; the day and the place agree.
